tonight.headline: Your 77% is four empty slots on the other roster, and they have been empty for three days.
body: Nothing has kicked off on either side. ESPN reads 121.1 to 70.8 and calls that 77%. The 70.8 is not a weak roster — it is an unset one. KEI returns have four unfilled starting slots as of this snapshot: both wide receiver spots, the defence and the kicker. George Pickens (14.8), Drake London (12.9), the 49ers defence (7.4) and Evan McPherson (7.9) are all sitting on their bench.

Fill those four and they read roughly 113.8 against your 121.1, which is a coin-flip decided by De'Von Achane and Cam Skattebo rather than a comfortable win. Nothing you do changes whether they set their lineup. What you can change is your own quarterback, and that window opens at 01:00 tomorrow — the card below.

case.label: What the 77% is actually measuring
case.body: ESPN's live model reads empty starting slots as zeros and does not assume a manager will fix them. That is correct behaviour and it is also why the number is not a lead. Every previous week this manager has eventually set a lineup.

case.label: Where you are genuinely ahead
case.body: Not in the empty slots. Jonathan Taylor at 88.7% snap share and 95.7% backfield touch share, and Saquon Barkley as the game-script back for a 7-point favourite, are two volume running backs against a roster whose best back is De'Von Achane in a 16.0-point implied Miami offence at San Francisco. That edge survives them filling the slots.

case.label: The overlap that hurts you
case.body: Jonathan Taylor and Rashee Rice are in the same Sunday night game, and De'Von Achane — theirs — is not. Your week resolves later and more correlated than theirs does, which is the one structural disadvantage in this matchup.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: KEI returns setting their lineup before 11:00 Sunday. If they do, treat this as a one-score game and the Stafford card below stops being an optimisation and starts being the margin.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Free at 01:00 Saturday Mexico City · do NOT claim before then
doFirst.title: At 01:00 Saturday, add Matthew Stafford free — drop MarShawn Lloyd
doFirst.subtitle: Raised from SOLID today. Nine hours from now the price on the best available quarterback drops from your entire season's waiver priority to nothing.

case.label: The clock, and why it is the headline
case.body: Stafford is on WAIVERS in this league until 07:00 UTC on 19 September, which is 01:00 Saturday in Mexico City. Claiming him before then spends waiver priority that NEVER resets in IPADE and drops Bloodsports from 3rd of 10 to last for the rest of the season. After 01:00, if nobody claims him, he is a free agent and costs a roster move and nothing else. You do not need to be awake: Saturday morning is inside the window.

case.label: The hole he fills
case.body: You have exactly one quarterback and he is QB15 on the board. Trevor Lawrence projects 14.9 this week and 282.0 on the season. Stafford projects 17.4 and 286.4 in this league's scoring. One injury or one bye and you are starting nobody.

case.label: The reporting, not the projection
case.body: FantasyLife name Stafford the single best quarterback streamer of Week 2, ahead of Geno Smith and Carson Wentz: reigning MVP, at home, with extra rest after international travel, against a Giants secondary their own writeup says was 'picked apart late in their opener'. Los Angeles carry a 28.0 implied total as 7.5-point favourites in a 48.5-point game — the best quarterback environment on Monday's card.

case.label: The drop, and why it is Lloyd and not Allgeier
case.body: MarShawn Lloyd averaged 2.8 yards per carry in Week 1 and Green Bay beat writers expect Kaleb Johnson, who took zero offensive snaps in Week 1, to absorb work at the Jets. Tyler Allgeier arrived at 16:29 this afternoon and reversing a move made six hours ago is exactly what STRATEGY section 3 forbids — so Lloyd remains the named drop even though he projects higher this week.

case.label: The second move nobody will tell you about
case.body: Adding him is only half. Jacksonville kick off at 14:05 Sunday and Los Angeles at 18:15 Monday, so if Stafford is on the roster you must move Lawrence to the bench and Stafford into the QB slot BEFORE 14:05 Sunday, or Lawrence locks in at 14.9 and Stafford's 17.4 sits behind him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Another IPADE manager claims Stafford at 07:00 UTC, which ends this at zero cost to you — three teams in this league carry a single quarterback and any of them could have a claim in. Or Team 13 accept the Lamar offer below, which delivers 312.9 instead of 286.4 and makes this card redundant. Or Los Angeles put Stafford on an injury report between now and Monday.

action.label: Add Matthew Stafford · drop MarShawn Lloyd

doFirst.title: Send Team 13 the Tuten-for-Lamar offer a ninth time, then stop
doFirst.subtitle: Downgraded from ELITE to SOLID and from EVEN to LONGSHOT. The trade is still correct; my read on their willingness was not.

case.label: Re-verified on this snapshot, not carried
case.body: Team 13 still hold Josh Allen at slot 0 — their starting quarterback, NOT being asked for — and Lamar Jackson at slot 20, their bench, in a one-QB league. Their running back room is Christian McCaffrey at 21.6, Blake Corum at 9.1 and Rachaad White at 7.6, and they must start two. That is the surplus and that is the hole, and both are unchanged since this morning.

case.label: Both sides, recomputed from scratch
case.body: Scored on both teams' optimal lineups on this 21:52 snapshot: you gain +5.9 this week and +16.0 on the season; they gain +1.0 this week and +40.6 on the season. Note the correction — this morning's brief published your season gain as +30.9, which failed to subtract Tuten's own contribution to your season-projected flex. +16.0 is the right number and the smaller one.

case.label: Why this chip and not Golden
case.body: The same search says giving Matthew Golden instead gains you MORE — +30.9 on the season — but gains them only +12.2 against Tuten's +40.6. Tuten is the offer that maximises their side, which is the offer that actually gets accepted, and Golden is your starting flex while Tuten is a bench back. If they counter asking for Golden, that deal is also good and you take it.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Eight sends, zero response, and no way to tell whether any of them were read — ESPN returns no trade-proposal state at all through this feed. Calling this EVEN for three days was a read on a manager who has given me no evidence, and eight unanswered offers IS evidence. It is LONGSHOT. Sending it a ninth time costs nothing but the message; a tenth starts to cost credibility for a deal you may actually want in week 9.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, which kills their +40.6. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report. Or there is no answer by Sunday 11:00, at which point this retires rather than being rewritten again.

whatWentWrong.title: You now carry four running backs and one quarterback, and the quarterback is QB15
whatWentWrong.lead: This afternoon's Allgeier-for-Charbonnet swap was the right move on its own terms and it deepened the position you are already longest in, on a roster missing a backup at the position that has no substitute.

case.label: How you got here
case.body: The 07:12 Wednesday transaction sent Matthew Stafford out for Zach Charbonnet. Charbonnet was OUT from the moment he arrived and was dropped at 16:29 today for Tyler Allgeier. Net effect of two days of moves: Stafford gone, a healthy fourth running back in his place.

case.label: What the Allgeier add got right
case.body: It cleared a dead seat at zero cost — Charbonnet was OUT with an indefinite shoulder and this league has no IR slot, so he was occupying a live bench place at a 0.0 projection. That needed doing and it got done.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: Nothing directly, but it used the seat that the Stafford card wanted. The drop is now MarShawn Lloyd rather than Charbonnet, and Lloyd projects 11.2 this week against Charbonnet's 0.0. The same recovery is now marginally more expensive than it was this morning.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley appears on a Sunday inactive list, the fourth running back stops being surplus and the Stafford card needs a different drop — at which point it becomes Michael Mayer, whose own condition is in Settled below.

whatWentWrong.title: I called the Lamar offer EVEN for three days on a manager who has never replied
whatWentWrong.lead: Eight sends, no response, no roster move. Odds is supposed to be a read on the other manager's willingness, and eight unanswered offers are the only evidence about willingness that exists.

case.label: What the label was doing
case.body: EVEN was a read on the trade's merit dressed up as a read on the person. The merit is real and unchanged — +40.6 to them on the season is the largest mutual-gain pair in this league. Their interest is a separate question and the answer has been silence.

case.label: Why it matters beyond this card
case.body: An honest odds label is the thing that tells you which offers to spend attention on. Three days of EVEN kept this card at the top of the brief and above a Stafford window that was always the more likely thing to actually happen.

case.label: What I cannot see, and am not hiding behind
case.body: ESPN returns no trade state through this feed — not sent, not read, not declined. That is a real limit. It is also not an excuse for labelling a silent counterparty EVEN eight times.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Any response at all from Team 13, including a decline, moves this back to EVEN, because a decline is information and silence is not. If Sunday arrives with no answer, it retires and does not get relabelled again.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +1.0 this week and +40.6 across the season, against your +5.9 and +16.0 — more than twice yours on the season, and putting that number in the message is what gets it read instead of ignored.

youGet.name: Lamar Jackson
youGet.detail: QB BAL · 20.8 this week, QB1 overall

case.label: Their structural surplus
case.body: Team 13 start Josh Allen at slot 0 and carry Lamar Jackson on their bench at slot 20 in a ONE-quarterback league. The second quarterback earns them nothing every week. STRATEGY section 7 names this exact shape as the thing to trade into.

case.label: Their actual hole
case.body: Christian McCaffrey at 21.6, Blake Corum at 9.1, Rachaad White at 7.6 — three backs, two required starters. Tuten at 10.1 displaces White immediately, which is where their +1.0 this week comes from, and 205.2 of season projection is where the +40.6 comes from.

case.label: What it does for you
case.body: Turns a bench running back into the highest-projected quarterback in football and fixes the one-quarterback problem without waiting for Stafford. +5.9 this week is Lamar 20.8 over Lawrence 14.9; you keep Lawrence as the backup rather than needing one.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: The deal only clears the bar comfortably on the season horizon; on the week it is +5.9 to you and +1.0 to them, and a manager reading only this week's numbers will see a lopsided ask. Say the season figure in the message. And be clear-eyed: eight sends have gone unanswered, so the base rate here is low.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, or move a quarterback, or Lamar appears on a Baltimore injury report. Also if they counter asking for Matthew Golden instead — take that deal, it gains you +30.9 on the season.

trades.copyText: Hi — would you do Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson? You're carrying two starting-calibre QBs in a one-QB league and only three RBs for two slots, so by my maths this is +40.6 season points for you against +16.0 for me. Tuten led the NFL in broken tackles in Week 1 and slots straight in ahead of Rachaad White. Happy to look at a different back on my side if Tuten isn't the one you want.

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: The named replacement if the Loveland thesis breaks on Sunday, still free, and his stock rose eleven places today on news that has nothing to do with him.

case.label: What changed today
case.body: Minnesota ruled Kyler Murray out and Jauan Jennings is out as well. Sports Illustrated move Hockenson from TE23 to TE14 on that alone, on the reasoning that Carson Wentz supports one receiver and a tight end rather than two receivers.

case.label: The role underneath it
case.body: He is Minnesota's number two target behind Jefferson at an 81% route share and 16% target share, ahead of every Minnesota receiver. In a league whose flex takes a tight end, that is a startable asset rather than a handcuff.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: The seat, not the player. Your five bench places hold the trade chip, the Stafford drop, a tight end whose job depends on Brock Bowers's knee, a receiver playing against your own defence, and a back who arrived six hours ago. There is no seat that can be spent on a second tight end today.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Colston Loveland drawing fewer than four targets against Minnesota on Sunday — the standing test on that thesis. If it fails, Hockenson takes the tight end slot directly, no waiver priority required, and the drop is Loveland himself.

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: The largest ownership anomaly on this wire — 82% rostered nationally, free here — and declined for a third consecutive run on an unchanged reason.

case.label: Why it keeps being declined
case.body: CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are both active and neither has appeared on a Dallas injury report. The third read in that passing game is not worth the last clean bench seat, whatever his national ownership says.

case.label: The number that argues for him
case.body: 167.4 season projection, second among tight ends on this wire behind nobody you can get, and Dallas carry a 27.25 implied total in the 50.5-point game that is the highest on the Week 2 board. If he were the first read this would be a card.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Lamb or Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report. He becomes the best free agent in this league the same hour and the seat is his.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on this wire, 77% rostered nationally and free here — and a thumb the market has not priced.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: Widely rostered elsewhere and free here is the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league per STRATEGY section 4, and this is the biggest instance of it on your receiver board by season projection.

case.label: The reason he is a watch, not a card
case.body: Jacksonville's final Friday report lists him limited all week with a thumb. He will play, per the same report. A thumb injury on a receiver is a catch-rate problem rather than an availability one, and his ownership is falling 0.60 a day rather than rising, which says the market is selling the injury rather than buying the role.

case.label: The structural caution
case.body: You already hold Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten from Jacksonville, and STRATEGY flags a week 7 Jaguars problem in this league specifically. A third Jaguar deepens a hole that is already on the calendar.

case.label: When to act
case.body: A clean Week 2 line with the thumb no longer on the report. If the Lamar trade lands, Tuten leaves and the Jacksonville concentration problem halves, which makes Meyers a straightforward add on the freed seat.

doNotChase.name: Zach Charbonnet
doNotChase.lead: You dropped him six hours ago and the price of changing your mind has gone up, not down. He is on WAIVERS now, so re-acquiring him costs your season's waiver priority.

case.label: What changed at 16:29
case.body: He came off your roster and onto the wire with status WAIVERS, clearing 07:00 UTC on 20 September. While he was yours he cost nothing to hold. Now he cannot be added as a free agent until Sunday morning, and before then only a claim reaches him.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: He is OUT with a shoulder described as indefinite, he started the season on the PUP list, and no dated return timeline has been published on any of four runs. Spending an IPADE waiver priority that never resets — dropping you from 3rd of 10 to last for the season — on a player with a 0.0 projection and no timeline is the single most expensive move available to you this week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Seattle publishing a dated return. If he is activated and practising, he is a free agent again on Sunday morning and can be re-added for nothing. Waiting costs you only the small risk that another manager claims an OUT running back, which nobody in this league has done.

doNotChase.name: Cam Little
doNotChase.lead: You dropped him at 07:06 yesterday and he is K3 on the board. Do not claim him back — that is the second most expensive move available to you this week.

case.label: Why it looks right
case.body: Pro Football Network have Little K3 and Jason Myers K9. On merit the swap was a downgrade of six places and that was logged as a mistake in yesterday's brief.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: He clears waivers at 07:00 UTC on 20 September, which means reaching him before Sunday's kickoffs requires a CLAIM. In this league that spends priority that never resets, for a kicker, which STRATEGY section 6 forbids by name: never a bye-week patch, never a handcuff, never a streamer. Six ranking places at kicker is worth perhaps a point a week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing this week. If he is still unowned after Sunday's games he is a free agent and the comparison reopens at zero cost on 22 September, when the seat's churn window also expires.

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: He is a better kicker than the one you have, he is free, and you should still not add him. Both halves of that sentence are the point.

case.label: The comparison, reported rather than skipped
case.body: PFN have Reichard K5 and Chase McLaughlin K6; both are free agents here. Jason Myers is K9. The upgrade costs no waiver priority. Minnesota also carry a 22.0 implied total against Seattle's 22.5, so the environment is a wash and the gap is the leg, not the offence.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Four ranking places at kicker is worth well under a point a week, and STRATEGY section 10 says not to propose a move worth under a point. Against that: this seat has already changed hands twice in 36 hours — Little out at 07:06, Myers in at 07:06 — and moving it a third time is the exact signature section 3 calls optimising noise.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty in Week 2 while Reichard or McLaughlin finish top five. The seat then reopens on 22 September when the churn window expires and the answer is whoever tops the Week 3 board.

settled.title: Label the Lamar offer EVEN for three consecutive runs (16–18 September)
settled.result: Wrong, and downgraded to LONGSHOT today. Eight sends with no response is the only evidence about this manager's willingness that exists, and I kept reporting the trade's merit as if it were his interest. The trade itself is unchanged and still correct.

settled.title: Publish your season gain on the Lamar trade as +30.9 (18 September, 07:30 run)
settled.result: Wrong arithmetic, corrected on this snapshot. +30.9 is Lamar's season projection minus Lawrence's and forgets that Tuten leaves your season-projected flex. Recomputed on both sides' optimal lineups the answer is +16.0 to you and +40.6 to them. The conclusion does not change; the number was overstated by nearly half.

settled.title: Hold Cam Little at kicker (16 September, held five consecutive runs)
settled.result: Broken by an owner move at 07:06 yesterday: Little out, Jason Myers in. PFN had Little K3 and Myers K9. No priority was spent, which is the part that was done right. Logged CHURN and closed, and the Do-not-chase row above exists so it does not get reversed at a much higher price.

settled.title: Claim Zach Charbonnet and drop Matthew Stafford (owner move, 07:12 Wednesday)
settled.result: Closed today. Charbonnet was OUT every day he was rostered and was dropped at 16:29 this afternoon for Tyler Allgeier, which recovers the seat. The Stafford half recovers at 01:00 tomorrow for nothing. Total cost of the round trip: two roster moves and one week of carrying a single quarterback.

settled.title: Keep Michael Mayer while Bowers is limited or out (14 September)
settled.result: Held, condition still true and checked on the live report rather than assumed. Brock Bowers is DOUBTFUL on the Raiders' Week 2 injury report after missing Wednesday and Thursday practice. A CBS headline saying Pete Carroll expects him to play turns out to be dated 14 September 2025 and was discarded rather than used.

settled.title: Hold Colston Loveland at tight end (16 September, unresolved for three runs)
settled.result: Held — and for the first time on evidence rather than on absence of evidence. Bleacher Nation's Week 1 tape review has him running a route on all 27 Chicago pass plays, used deliberately as a decoy to pull coverage off Cole Kmet. The zero was scheme. The four-target test still resolves on Sunday.

settled.title: Start Matthew Golden in the RB/WR/TE flex over Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Held and confirmed on a fresh number: a 26.2% target share and 95 receiving yards in Week 1, with FantasyPros calling him a strong flex despite the Jets' two-high shell. The 'fewer than five targets' clause has no support in anything published this week.

settled.title: Watch Tyler Allgeier rather than roster him (18 September, 07:30 run)
settled.result: Overtaken by the owner at 16:29 and that is fine — the watch row existed to make the add defensible and it was. The caveat the row would have carried arrived Friday: Mike LaFleur says 'they are going to rotate', and Jeremiyah Love took the Week 1 touchdown. Lead back overstates it.

settled.title: Add the Ravens defence as a free agent and drop the Jaguars (16 September)
settled.result: Held, and improved. Trey Hendrickson was back at practice Friday. New Orleans carry an 18.75 implied total as 8.5-point underdogs. No priority was spent and none should ever be on a defence in this league.

settled.title: Decline Jake Ferguson even once he became free (17 September)
settled.result: Held for a third run. Lamb and Pickens are both active and off the injury report, his ownership is falling, and the third read in Dallas is not worth the last clean seat.

settled.title: Decline T.J. Hockenson on the seat rather than the player (17 September)
settled.result: Held, with the player's stock explicitly rising against it. Murray out moves him TE23 to TE14. The decline is about having no seat, and that is still true today — but it is now a decline against a better player than it was yesterday, which is worth saying out loud.

settled.title: Do not offer Garrett Wilson for Josh Allen (16 September)
settled.result: Held. Allen is still Team 13's slot-0 starter. The exhaustive pair search re-run on this snapshot surfaces it again as the largest mutual-gain pair in the league at +21.3 to you and +21.8 to them, and it is still not to be sent — STRATEGY's untouchable rule names this exact failure.

settled.title: Hold Jason Myers rather than move the kicker seat a third time (18 September)
settled.result: Held on the same reasoning fifteen hours later. Reichard K5 and McLaughlin K6 are free and both beat Myers K9; the gain is under a point and the seat has changed hands twice in 36 hours. Reported rather than skipped, which is the point.

cannotSee.label: Whether Stafford clears at 01:00 Saturday or is claimed first
cannotSee.body: Rivals' pending claims are invisible — ESPN only ever returns your own. Three IPADE teams carry a single quarterback and any of them could have a claim in on the best quarterback on this wire. If he is gone at 07:00 UTC, the card costs you nothing and the answer becomes Bo Nix at 83.9% rostered and free, or Jared Goff on waivers clearing 23 September.

cannotSee.label: Whether Team 13 have read any of the nine offers
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns no trade-proposal state through this feed at all — not sent, not read, not declined. Eight sends have produced no visible response and no roster move on their side. I have downgraded the odds on that silence, but I genuinely cannot distinguish 'declined' from 'never opened'.

cannotSee.label: Whether KEI returns will set their lineup, which is the entire 77%
cannotSee.body: Four starting slots are empty on their side as of 21:52 UTC and have been for three days. Filling them with the four best players on their bench takes them from 70.8 to roughly 113.8 against your 121.1. I cannot see their intent and ESPN's model does not guess at it.

cannotSee.body: Colston Loveland, Michael Mayer and Tyler Allgeier. I did not retrieve a points-allowed-by-position figure for Minnesota's, the Chargers' or Seattle's defences this run. cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, which undercuts the trade arithmetic
cannotSee.body: seasonProj has produced identical figures across snapshots on four consecutive days. They do differ correctly between the two leagues — Stafford reads 286.4 here and 303.4 in Chem — so the scoring maths is live even if the forecast is not. The +40.6 and +16.0 in the trade card are therefore August's opinion of these players, priced precisely.

cannotSee.label: Whether the Allgeier add changes the Stafford drop
cannotSee.body: I have decided it does not — Lloyd stays the named drop because reversing a six-hour-old move is what STRATEGY section 3 exists to prevent. But Lloyd projects 11.2 this week against Allgeier's 7.1, so on this week's numbers alone the other answer is defensible. I am choosing the rule over the point, and saying so.
